docs.title: Ari Grain Quay
docs.text: Ari Grain Quay handles much of Ari’s grain and fish traffic. Harlan Vey maintains an office close enough to the scales that merchants cannot easily avoid him.

docs.title: Everyday Use
docs.text: Trade here follows the rhythms of arrivals and departures rather than a fixed modern schedule. Prices can change sharply when a caravan, fishing fleet, or shipment is late, and local information often moves between stalls faster than it reaches any official notice board.

docs.title: The Copper Gull
docs.text: The Copper Gull is a busy Ari inn shared by fishers, grain merchants, and prospectors. The common room displays ore samples beside mounted fish, and arguments about which profession lies more are never resolved.

docs.title: Everyday Use
docs.text: The establishment serves as more than a place to drink or sleep. Travelers use it to hear road conditions, find temporary help, arrange meetings, and learn which local businesses are actually open to strangers.

docs.title: Vytung Yard
docs.text: Vytung Yard is the inland supply market of Ari, where pack animals, rope, tools, lamps, food, and hirelings are gathered for mining trips toward Vy’Tungavor.

docs.title: Everyday Use
docs.text: Trade here follows the rhythms of arrivals and departures rather than a fixed modern schedule. Prices can change sharply when a caravan, fishing fleet, or shipment is late, and local information often moves between stalls faster than it reaches any official notice board.

docs.title: Harlan Vey
docs.text:
Harlan Vey is Harbor Warden of Ari.

He comes from a fishing family but now spends most of his time mediating between fishers, grain factors, coastal captains, and prospectors moving toward Vy’Tungavor.

Harlan has little patience for mining schemes that expect Ari to supply food and guards on credit.

docs.title: Manner
docs.text: Harlan is plain-spoken and most comfortable on the working waterfront. He gives miners and captains the same treatment: pay what is owed, do not endanger the town, and do not expect Ari to finance a risky plan just because it sounds profitable.

docs.title: Brynk
docs.text:
Brynk is a small and peculiar mountain town whose isolation has preserved laws, rituals, and customs that often seem baffling to outsiders.

The settlement sits high in the southern range and does not encourage casual immigration.

docs.title: Character
docs.text: Brynk is quiet, enclosed, and deliberate. Doors are painted with family marks, public behavior is tightly regulated by custom, and visitors are expected to learn local rules quickly rather than plead ignorance later.

docs.title: Government
docs.text:
The town is governed by a closed council of established households. Vessa Keln serves as the current Voice of Brynk, but the title grants less personal freedom than outsiders assume.

Brynk recognizes the Crown in principle while insisting that local customary law governs nearly everything within its walls.

docs.title: Trade and Economy
docs.text:
Brynk trades selectively in mountain herbs, wool, preserved foods, stonework, and a few specialized crafts.

The town’s small population means it relies on periodic caravans for salt, metal goods, grain, and luxuries.

docs.title: Travel and Connections
docs.text:
Soryn’s Crossing lies roughly 40-50 road miles away: 2-3 days walking, 3-4 by wagon, about 2 days mounted, or less than a day by griffin.

The mountain climb raises the price of cheap bulky goods and helps preserve Brynk’s isolation. See Saros - Distances, Travel, Trade, and Population for the canonical route model.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: The mountain itself provides much of Brynk’s defense. Narrow approaches, watch posts, and a population that knows every local trail make surprise attack difficult.

docs.title: Places of Interest
docs.text:
• The Closed Gate — the formal entrance where visitors receive local rules
  • House of Measures — civic hall and court of custom
  • The Quiet Cup — the only inn routinely permitted to host outsiders

docs.title: NPCs Found Here
docs.text: NPC Race Building Factions Vessa Keln Human House of Measures

docs.title: House of Measures
docs.text: The House of Measures is Brynk’s civic hall and court of customary law. Vessa Keln speaks for the council here, though many hearings are decided by precedent older than anyone present.

docs.title: Public Use
docs.text: Most residents encounter the building through ordinary civic business rather than ceremony. Notices, disputes, permits, records, and requests for local officials all pass through it, making the place a useful measure of what the settlement currently considers important.

docs.title: The Closed Gate
docs.text: The Closed Gate is the formal entrance to Brynk. Visitors are stopped here, recorded, and given a concise explanation of the local customs they will be expected to follow.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: The structure is part of the settlement’s ordinary defensive routine, not merely a wartime monument. Watch rotations, inspections, signal procedures, and emergency stores are maintained even during quiet seasons.

docs.title: Visitor Custom
docs.text:
A gate clerk records names, purpose, intended lodging, and any weapons a visitor openly carries.

The rules given to outsiders can seem overly specific, but locals regard the briefing as a courtesy: once a person has been told the customs, claiming ignorance later carries little weight.

docs.title: The Quiet Cup
docs.text: The Quiet Cup is the only inn in Brynk routinely permitted to host outsiders. Its rules are posted prominently, and the proprietor expects them to be read rather than debated.

docs.title: Everyday Use
docs.text: The establishment serves as more than a place to drink or sleep. Travelers use it to hear road conditions, find temporary help, arrange meetings, and learn which local businesses are actually open to strangers.

docs.title: House Rules
docs.text:
Conversation is welcome; public disruption is not.

The innkeeper keeps a copy of Brynk’s visitor customs behind the bar and will explain them once without complaint. A second explanation is usually shorter.

The Quiet Cup therefore becomes the place where outsiders quietly ask what a local rule actually means before testing it in public.

docs.title: Vessa Keln
docs.text:
Vessa Keln serves as the Voice of Brynk, speaking publicly for the closed council of established households.

The office makes her visible but does not make her an absolute ruler. Brynk’s customary law binds the Voice as tightly as it binds visitors.

Vessa is formal, controlled, and surprisingly helpful to outsiders who make an honest effort to follow local rules. Deliberate disrespect for Brynk’s customs is one of the few things that can make her openly angry.

docs.title: Manner
docs.text: Vessa never apologizes for Brynk’s customs. She does, however, distinguish sharply between an outsider who makes an honest mistake and one who decides local law is beneath them.

docs.title: Dun Karag
docs.text:
Dun Karag is a Thar’um stronghold at Hex 53.85, where the road north from Skaggerty reaches The Masys Mountains. Its gates control the maintained passage under and through the range toward Caelum’s End.

It is the last settled civilization before the cold, dead north.

docs.title: The Northern Gate
docs.text:
The Thar’um maintain avalanche walls, tunnel lamps, bridgeworks, way-markers, ventilation shafts, and refuge chambers along the mountain passage. They also close the road without apology when weather, monsters, or deeper dangers make travel suicidal.

Anyone determined to go north must deal with the hold. Travelers are questioned about purpose, provisions, weapons, and expected return. Passage may require a toll, a guide, repair work, news from the south, or a sworn promise to leave sealed doors alone.

docs.title: Travel and Connections
docs.text:
The maintained southern road descends toward Skaggerty. Northward, the Thar’um-controlled passage continues through The Masys Mountains toward Caelum’s End. Weather, closures, and required guides matter more than a simple mileage estimate, and no dependable commercial travel time has yet been fixed.

See Saros - Distances, Travel, Trade, and Population for the current map scale and overland assumptions.

docs.title: Government
docs.text:
A council of gate wardens, engineers, brewers, quartermasters, and elder delvers governs the hold. Offices rotate by craft and season; outsiders rarely learn which councillor carries the greatest private influence.

The hold trades with Saros but does not recognize Crown officers as commanders within its gates.

docs.title: Deepmantle Ale
docs.text: Dun Karag produces Deepmantle Ale, a dark, cold-fermented ale aged in stone-lined vaults. Many drinkers call it the finest ale in Saros. Genuine casks bear a Thar’um chisel mark under the bung, a detail frequently missed by southern counterfeiters.

docs.title: Character
docs.text: The stronghold is warm, disciplined, and never fully quiet. Chain lifts, water wheels, distant hammers, and gate bells echo through carved halls. Hospitality is serious once granted; so is a closed door.

docs.title: Goslow
docs.text:
Goslow is the largest concentration of permanent residents in known Saros and the realm’s dominant commercial port. It sits on the inner coast of Bishop’s Bay, where the sheltered water, nearby farmland, fishing grounds, and roads converging on the bay have made trade more dependable than almost anywhere else in the north.

Large ships entering Bishop’s Bay usually anchor outside the most difficult approaches and lighter vessels finish the run toward Goslow’s docks. Cargo arriving by road, river, and sea changes hands constantly, and people from every major faction eventually pass through the city.

The city is also the ordinary gateway to Pyrris. Travelers bound for the capital leave Goslow by The High Road, the immense switchback road climbing the sheer cliffs above Bishop’s Bay.

docs.title: Character
docs.text:
Goslow feels busy even when nothing important is happening. Dock bells, carts, arguments, gulls, smith-work, tavern music, and shouted prices blend into a permanent background noise.

It is wealthy by Sarosian standards but not polished. Old mansions stand beside ropewalks and warehouses; guild offices share streets with cramped boarding houses; the harbor districts never entirely stop working.

docs.title: Government
docs.text:
Goslow operates under a royal charter. A civic council handles ordinary taxation, markets, streets, docks, sanitation, and commercial disputes, while Crown magistrates retain authority over serious royal law.

The Aegis Legion keeps its principal local garrison at Duskpoint under Vostin The Mighty. The Legion is powerful, especially while Queen Amara is missing, but it is not technically the civil government of Goslow.

The city’s merchants and guilds possess enough economic weight that even the Crown normally negotiates before disrupting the docks.

docs.title: Trade and Economy
docs.text:
Goslow’s economy is unusually broad:

  • Fishing and coastal trade
  • Grain, vegetables, livestock, and nearby agriculture, including the Skaggerty farm belt
  • Fresh, smoked, salted, and preserved seafood from Bishop’s Bay
  • Shipbuilding and repair
  • Rope, sailcloth, pitch, timber, and chandlery
  • Smithing and specialist craftwork
  • Inns, taverns, gambling, warehousing, and finance
  • Trade moving between Port Quartz, Kylor, Pyrris, and southern Saros

The Bulkhead and Aucien Shipyard are major parts of the shipbuilding trade. Bedford’s Forge is famous for high-end metalwork and the rare ability to work Fey-stone.

docs.title: Food and Provisions
docs.text:
Goslow does not survive on grain alone. Bishop’s Bay supplies fresh fish and other seafood, while smoking, salting, and preservation make part of that catch suitable for ships, garrisons, winter stores, and the climb to Pyrris.

Grain remains important for bread, porridge, brewing, animal feed, and military provisioning. Much of it comes from nearby farms and the wider agricultural belt organized through Skaggerty, with additional food arriving by coast and southern trade.

This mixed supply network makes a poor harvest dangerous without making any single small town solely responsible for feeding fourteen thousand residents.

docs.title: Travel and Connections
docs.text:
Destination Route Working Distance and Time Kylor Road or coastal vessel 45-50 miles; 2-3 days walking, 3-4 by heavy wagon, about 1 day by sea Skaggerty Western pocket road 40-55 miles; 2-3 days walking or 3-4 by grain wagon Pyrris The High Road 35-40 miles; about 2 days walking or 2-3 by loaded wagon Port Quartz Ship through Bishop’s Bay and upriver 70-90 water miles; ordinarily 2-3 days outward and 1-2 days returning

There is no ordinary safe commercial road from Goslow to Port Quartz. See Saros - Distances, Travel, Trade, and Population for the canonical route model.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Goslow has its own watch, gated walls, harbor patrols, and substantial militia potential. Duskpoint gives the Legion a permanent military presence immediately outside the city.

Griffin patrols under Vostin are a familiar sight around Goslow and the approaches to Pyrris.

The city’s size makes it safer than most Sarosian settlements, but no one mistakes that safety for control of the wilderness beyond its roads.

docs.title: Places of Interest
docs.text:
• The Toad — the city’s largest and most famous inn, operated by Perla Mudridge and Gerdga
  • The Silver Drake — a major Gambler’s Guild hall and bank
  • The Sphinx’s Spellbook — cramped apothecary and arcane shop owned by Mori
  • Bedford’s Forge — renowned smithy operated by Bedford and Mary
  • The Bulkhead — the Aucien family’s rope and shipbuilding business
  • Aucien Shipyard — the family’s larger coastal yard outside the main gates
  • Temple of Torm — temple, library, and home of Korth and Ostalda
  • Duskpoint — the local Aegis Legion garrison
  • The Storm Runner — the vessel captained by Mirken Stanton and navigated by Breelyn

Approximate permanent structures: 1,385.

docs.title: Aucien Shipyard
docs.text:
Aucien Shipyard is the principal Aucien family marina and shipyard on Bishop’s Bay, just north of the main walls of Goslow.

The yard is larger and rougher than the family’s in-town business at The Bulkhead.

docs.title: Work
docs.text:
The shipyard handles:

  • Hull repair
  • Small-vessel construction
  • Rigging replacement
  • Timber storage
  • Haul-out work
  • Dock space
  • Custom marine jobs

The family’s rope and shipbuilding experience allows work to move between the yard and the Bulkhead depending on the size of the job.

docs.title: Position
docs.text: Its location outside the main gates gives the yard more shoreline and working space than could be found inside Goslow, but it also means the family must take its own security seriously after dark.

docs.title: Bedford's Forge
docs.text:
Known for the finest craftsmanship this side of Vy’Tungavor, Bedford’s Forge is the local Goslow smithy where you can get anything you desire made if you are willing to both pay the high price, and wait patiently on the list behind high-priority clientele. Heat bellows out of the doorway and permeates the entire colossal structure of The Forge. Many humans tend to the forges that fill the interior, and the sounds of metal being worked drowns out all but the loudest voices.

Overseeing the forge is a massive man simply known as Bedford, one of the few known beings in Saros capable of working Fey-stone into useable weapons and armor.

docs.title: Swords = 5000gp + 1 Month
docs.text:
• +1 Sword of Might
  • +1 Sword of Accuracy
  • +1 Sword of Flame

docs.title: Duskpoint
docs.text:
Duskpoint is the main Aegis Legion garrison serving Goslow and the surrounding roads.

Vostin The Mighty commands the post.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Duskpoint functions as:

  • Barracks
  • Armory
  • Local military headquarters
  • Jail for serious Crown offenses
  • Patrol staging point
  • Griffin roost and landing ground
  • Administrative office for Legion business around Goslow

docs.title: Relationship with Goslow
docs.text:
Duskpoint lies outside the city walls rather than at the civic center.

That separation reflects an important distinction: the Legion is extraordinarily powerful in Goslow, but it is not the same institution as the city’s civil government.

Vostin’s griffin patrols regularly depart from Duskpoint toward Pyrris, The High Road, and the roads around the bay.

docs.title: Griffin Roost
docs.text:
The roost supports the bonded companions of Griffin Riders, not a pool of interchangeable mounts. Riders and griffins are quartered close together, and every patrol pair maintains its own tack, habits, feeding routine, and resting space.

The animals’ food requirements make the roost one of Duskpoint’s largest recurring expenses. Fishing contracts, livestock offal, butchers, handlers, drainage crews, and secure storage tie the garrison directly to Goslow’s harbor and markets.

docs.title: Temple of Torm
docs.text:
Temple of Torm is one of the most respected religious buildings in Goslow, serving as a temple, library, place of counsel, and refuge.

Korth is the elderly head priest.

Ostalda lives in a small chamber connected to the temple library and works there as a sage and diviner.

docs.title: Korth
docs.text:
Korth is now famous for falling asleep at inconvenient moments, but older residents still tell stories of the paladin who rallied Goslow against a major orc raid.

His age has diminished his stamina more than his reputation.

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
The temple library contains:

  • Religious works
  • Local histories
  • Old travel accounts
  • Copies of legal and civic records
  • Material collected by priests and adventurers

Ostalda’s presence has also made it a place people visit when ordinary scholarship is not enough.

docs.title: The Bulkhead
docs.text:
The Bulkhead is the Aucien family’s long-running rope and shipbuilding business in Goslow.

Jarvis Aucien oversees the shop.

docs.title: Work
docs.text:
The Bulkhead specializes in:

  • Rope
  • Rigging
  • Blocks and tackle
  • Sail and line repair
  • Ship fittings
  • Small marine construction
  • Contract work for larger vessels

Large hull work can be transferred to Aucien Shipyard outside the city walls.

docs.title: Family Business
docs.text:
The business has passed through the Aucien family for generations and is closely associated with Goslow’s working waterfront.

Jarvis’s size, blond hair, and muscular build make him difficult to miss in a shop already full of coils, spars, timber, and dockworkers.

docs.title: The Silver Drake
docs.text:
The Silver Drake is Goslow’s sole Guild-chartered gambling hall and a Bank of Saros. It is one of the most famous halls in Saros, surpassed in scale by The Golden Goose in Rore.

Lone-Wolf Louie oversees the hall.

docs.title: Gambling
docs.text:
The Drake attracts travelers willing to risk serious coin.

Licensed tables, private games, tournaments, and high-value wagers all operate under Guild rules.

Cheating that threatens the hall’s reputation is treated much more seriously than simply losing badly.

docs.title: Banking
docs.text:
The Silver Drake also provides secure financial services.

Merchants and adventurers can deposit coin, arrange withdrawals, and use the Drake’s reputation to avoid carrying their entire wealth on dangerous roads.

Individual account balances are private records and are not publicly posted.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
The building is tightly controlled.

Door staff, house guards, secure counting rooms, and Guild connections make robbery a much worse idea than the concentration of money might initially suggest.

docs.title: The Sphinx's Spellbook
docs.text:
The Sphinx’s Spellbook is an old, narrow two-story apothecary and arcane shop only a short walk from the Goslow docks.

The cracked stone building is threaded with roots and vines that seem to have grown through it rather than around it.

docs.title: Interior
docs.text:
Incense, herbal smoke, dust, parchment, potion bottles, books, charms, and strange collected objects fill almost every available surface.

A narrow path through the clutter eventually reaches a small counter and bell.

docs.title: Mori
docs.text:
Mori owns the shop.

She is a timid but extremely intelligent young half-elf with purple hair and alchemical tattoos covering much of her visible skin.

Mori lives above the shop with Chibs, a penguin she rescued injured and alone near Bishop’s Bay.

She crafted the small frost-rune pendant Chibs wears to help keep him comfortable in Goslow’s climate.

docs.title: Goods
docs.text:
The Spellbook is a place to look for:

  • Herbs
  • Alchemical ingredients
  • Minor magical supplies
  • Unusual books
  • Potions
  • Oddments collected from travelers

What Mori actually has in stock changes constantly.

docs.title: The Storm Runner
docs.text:
The Storm Runner is a small troop transport captained by Mirken Stanton and navigated by Breelyn.

The vessel carries a working crew of roughly one hundred and has a reputation for surviving coastal and river voyages that more cautious captains decline.

docs.title: Crew
docs.text:
Mirken commands the ship with a mixture of confidence, aggression, and personal loyalty to his people.

Breelyn, his childhood friend and navigator, is regarded by Mirken as the finest reader of the waters and stars he has ever known.

docs.title: Reputation
docs.text:
The Storm Runner is associated with hard sailing, dangerous routes, and a crew that does not particularly enjoy being ordered around by the Aegis Legion.

Mirken’s open hostility toward Admiral Thainan is well known among people familiar with the ship.

docs.title: The Toad
docs.text:
The Toad is a two-story half-timber and brick building with smooth stone floors and a warm breeze from the massive blazing fireplace that invites the weary traveler inside on a cold evening. The largest and busiest tavern and Inn in Goslow, filled with elf-wrought tables and chairs, it was once a massive mansion that fell to ruin with age and was bought and restored by Perla. The main hall houses a large collection of priceless artwork from all across Saros. Accommodations range from small, modestly priced rooms with a soft woolen mattress, to huge luxury suites that rival small houses.

The owner and innkeeper of the Toad is a tall female halfling named Perla. She was once an adventurer, but was maimed by a dragon and lost her left leg. She loves details and rumors, and she’s often seen sitting at a table sharing tall drinks and even taller tales with adventurers that come into the Toad.

The inn’s manager is a stocky female halfling named Gerdga. She has a heavy smoker’s cough, a dry sarcastic wit, and she insists on inspecting every coin paid to her. Anything you need can either be found behind her bar or by her hard working crew.

Employees: Hob - Bound water elemental who works as bouncer and cleaner. Lommen and Hommen - gnome twins given a job by Perla after they were rescued. Munchies Muldridge - Nephew of Gerdga and general clumsy fool.

Menu: Baked Goose and Onion, Glass of Mead (1 sp) Baked Shrimp and Almond Bread, Glass of Wine (2 sp) Vegetable soup and Garlic Bread, Choice of Wine (2 sp) Baked Phoenix and Boysenberry Tart, Glass of Brunae (3 sp)

Rooms: (per night) Modest (1 sp) = 6 Accommodating (5 sp) = 10 Luxurious (1 gp) = 4 Suite (5 gp) = 2

(Longer term housing is also available by speaking with Perla.)

docs.title: Bedford
docs.text: Overseeing Bedford’s Forge is a massive man simply known as Bedford. He has a loud booming voice, a shiny bald head, and a large grey mustache. He and his wife Mary love visitors and they are always cheerful. His leather overalls are covered in soot and burn marks and his hands are like chiseled steel from decades of dedicated smith-work. Though very bulky and freakishly strong, he is also a proficient artist who adorns his creations with delicate and detailed inlays. He is one of the few beings in all of Saros capable of forging Fey-stone.

docs.title: Breelyn
docs.text:
Breelyn is the navigator of The Storm Runner and has been Mirken Stanton’s closest friend since childhood.

Where Mirken is loud, confrontational, and instinctive, Breelyn is the person who can look at stars, current, wind, shoreline, and weather and turn all of it into a route. Mirken openly considers her the finest navigator he has ever known and would risk almost anything for her.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Breelyn is brilliant at sea and spectacularly unreliable in port.

She is a colossal drunkard with a talent for disappearing into taverns, gaming halls, and back rooms for days at a time. When the Storm Runner is due to sail, Mirken and his crew sometimes have to search half the harbor district to find her.

The crew treats this less like an emergency than an annoying maritime tradition.

docs.title: Skill
docs.text:
Breelyn’s knowledge of the waters and stars of Saros is exceptional. She can judge currents, identify unfamiliar coastlines, and navigate by celestial patterns that most captains would not trust themselves to read.

Her drinking has damaged her reputation ashore far more than it has diminished the respect sailors have for her.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: Mirken Stanton is not merely her captain. The two have known one another since childhood, and their loyalty to each other predates the Storm Runner itself.

docs.title: Chibs
docs.text:
Chibs is the tiny penguin who lives with Mori above The Sphinx’s Spellbook in Goslow.

Mori found him alone, injured, and badly out of place near Bishop’s Bay several years ago. She nursed him back to health and eventually built a small frost-rune pendant that helps keep his body cool in Goslow’s climate.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Chibs waddles freely through the shop and has learned exactly which shelves he is allowed to bump into without causing a disaster.

The pendant leaves him cool enough that small beads of condensation and meltwater sometimes appear where he has been sitting.

Regular customers tend to know Chibs almost as well as they know Mori.

docs.title: Reputation
docs.text:
Nobody agrees how a penguin ended up alone in Bishop’s Bay.

Mori has stopped pretending she knows.

docs.title: Gerdga
docs.text:
Gerdga is the manager of The Toad and the person most likely to actually know what is happening inside the enormous inn at any given moment.

She is a short halfling with a deep raspy voice, a terrible smoker’s cough, and a dry sarcasm that regulars learn to appreciate or at least survive.

docs.title: Habits
docs.text:
Gerdga is usually seen with:

  • A pipe in one hand
  • A magnifying glass close by
  • A ledger she insists nobody else keeps correctly

She examines every unfamiliar coin before accepting it and has embarrassed more than one traveler who tried to pass damaged or questionable currency.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
Perla Mudridge is Gerdga’s closest friend as well as the owner of The Toad.

Gerdga manages staff, tabs, supplies, complaints, and most practical problems so Perla can spend more time talking to guests and collecting stories.

docs.title: Hob
docs.text:
Hob is an eight-foot-tall water elemental bound to The Toad in Goslow.

He works as cleaner, servant, and bouncer.

docs.title: Work
docs.text:
At Gerdga’s instruction, Hob can:

  • Sweep spilled drink and dirt into his own body
  • Wash tables and floors
  • Carry heavy objects
  • Separate fighting customers
  • Remove unruly patrons from the building

Despite being made of water, he leaves remarkably little moisture behind unless he intends to.

docs.title: Nature
docs.text:
Hob does not appear to possess ordinary human desires or ambitions.

He is a magical construct or bound elemental tied directly to the premises. If forced beyond the limits of The Toad, his form collapses into ordinary water.

Regular customers have learned that arguing with Hob is useless.

Arguing with Gerdga about why Hob threw someone out is only slightly more productive.

docs.title: Jarvis Aucien
docs.text: Jarvis Aucien is a tall, blonde, and muscular Half-Elf who operates The Bulkhead in Goslow, a family rope and ship making business that has been passed down the Aucien line for generations. The Bulkhead is where anyone seeking the finest sea-faring vessels in all of Saros go, with hopes that they have enough coin, and that Jarvis’ services aren’t booked out more than a few months. There is also quite the ropemaking operation as well, situated right on the docks. The actual Aucien Shipyard is just outside the gates of Goslow on the coast of Bishop’s Bay to the north.

docs.title: Korth
docs.text:
Korth is the head priest at Temple of Torm in Goslow.

He is a very old human paladin with enormous white eyebrows that nearly hide his eyes and a frustrating tendency to fall asleep in the middle of quiet conversations.

docs.title: Past
docs.text:
Older Goslow residents remember a very different Korth.

Local stories credit him with rallying defenders during a major orc raid and holding the town together when panic might otherwise have broken its defenses.

Whether every heroic detail is accurate, nobody disputes that he fought.

docs.title: Present
docs.text:
Age has made Korth slow and frequently narcoleptic, but it has not made him foolish.

When awake, he is patient, difficult to shock, and unusually good at separating a genuine moral problem from an adventurer’s attempt to have a priest approve something reckless.

He works closely with Ostalda, the temple’s resident sage.

docs.title: Lone-Wolf Louie
docs.text:
Lone-Wolf Louie oversees The Silver Drake, the famous Gambler’s Guild hall and bank in Goslow.

He speaks with a heavy accent and is almost always chewing something, which makes him difficult to understand even when he is trying to be clear.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Louie supervises:

  • Gaming-floor staff
  • House security
  • High-value disputes
  • Banking operations
  • Large withdrawals
  • Relationships with the Gambler’s Guild

He rarely deals cards himself anymore.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Louie gives the impression of being distracted until money or cheating is involved.

At that point he becomes extremely precise.

He likes regular customers who lose gracefully, distrusts people who win too loudly, and has no patience for anyone who treats a Guild hall like an unprotected tavern game.

docs.title: Mary
docs.text:
Mary is the wife of Bedford and a familiar presence around Bedford’s Forge in Goslow.

She has a small-town warmth that feels strangely out of place beside one of the busiest and hottest smithies in the city.

docs.title: Daily Life
docs.text:
Mary enjoys:

  • Raising butterflies
  • Beekeeping
  • Playing cards in the shade
  • Gossiping with friends
  • Reading The Fine Point gazette
  • Drinking lemonade while Bedford works

She is not a smith, but she knows the Forge’s clients, schedules, and personalities well enough to notice problems before many apprentices do.

docs.title: Ambition
docs.text:
Mary has an enduring fascination with legendary magical decks and openly dreams of one day drawing from a Deck of Many Things.

Bedford considers this one of the few topics on which his wife has completely lost her good sense.

docs.title: Mirken Stanton
docs.text:
Mirken Stanton is captain of The Storm Runner, a small troop transport with a working crew of roughly one hundred.

He has a reputation for being fearless at sea, fair enough to his own people, and frighteningly quick to fight when someone threatens a member of his crew.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Mirken is blunt, proud, and difficult to intimidate. He enjoys insulting authority almost as much as he enjoys surviving things sensible captains avoid.

He has little affection for pirates, but his hatred of The Aegis Legion runs deeper—especially where Admiral Thainan is concerned.

docs.title: Breelyn
docs.text:
Breelyn has been Mirken’s best friend since childhood and now serves as his navigator. He considers her irreplaceable.

Her habit of vanishing into taverns and gambling houses whenever the ship is in port drives him mad, but any outsider who mistakes his complaints for permission to mistreat her learns very quickly how protective he is.

docs.title: Reputation at Sea
docs.text:
Mirken claims to have killed more dragon turtles than any living captain in Saros. Whether the count is accurate depends heavily on who is buying the drinks.

He is also obsessed with the legendary Golden Grouper and has sworn that one day the Storm Runner will bring it home.

docs.title: Enemies
docs.text: Mirken considers Admiral Thainan a sworn enemy. Their hostility goes well beyond ordinary disagreement with the Legion.

docs.title: Mori
docs.text:
Mori owns The Sphinx’s Spellbook, the cramped apothecary and arcane shop near the docks of Goslow.

She is a short young half-elf with purple hair and alchemical tattoos across much of her visible skin, leaving her face comparatively unmarked.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Mori is timid around forceful strangers but becomes much more confident when discussing herbs, alchemy, magical ingredients, or unusual physical effects.

She is far more intelligent than her nervous manner initially suggests.

docs.title: Work
docs.text:
Mori buys, studies, and sells:

  • Herbs
  • Reagents
  • Potions
  • Minor charms
  • Unusual books
  • Collected magical oddities

Her stock changes constantly because travelers bring her things she has never seen before.

docs.title: Chibs
docs.text:
Mori lives above the shop with Chibs, the penguin she rescued near Bishop’s Bay.

She created his frost-rune pendant herself.

docs.title: Munchies Muldridge
docs.text:
Munchil “Munchies” Muldridge works at The Toad in Goslow.

He is the nephew of Perla Mudridge and has spent much of his life surrounded by adventurers, which has convinced him that he should obviously become one.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Munchies is enthusiastic, clumsy, easily distracted, and not especially bright.

He volunteers for jobs before understanding them and has an impressive ability to turn a simple errand into something Perla eventually has to fix.

docs.title: At the Toad
docs.text:
His duties change according to whatever Gerdga believes he can perform without damaging furniture.

He carries luggage, clears tables, runs messages, helps in the stable, and occasionally disappears because he decided to “practice adventuring.”

Most regulars like him.

Very few would trust him with a secret route, expensive potion, or lit torch.

docs.title: Ostalda
docs.text:
Ostalda is the resident sage at Temple of Torm in Goslow.

She lives in a small room attached to the temple library.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text:
Ostalda is a dark-haired half-elf whose skin has developed a noticeable blue cast after years of ritual divination involving sacred mushrooms.

The effect has become so associated with her that strangers occasionally assume it is natural.

docs.title: Work
docs.text:
Ostalda studies:

  • Old texts
  • Religious lore
  • Strange magical phenomena
  • Dreams and visions
  • Historical accounts
  • Questions ordinary priests would rather refer elsewhere

She is not a convenient source of perfect answers.

Her value lies in recognizing patterns and identifying when an apparently isolated event resembles something older.

docs.title: Korth
docs.text: She works closely with Korth, though she has learned to continue reading while he sleeps through portions of their conversations.

docs.title: Perla Mudridge
docs.text:
Perla Mudridge owns The Toad, the largest and busiest inn in Goslow.

She is a tall halfling and former adventurer whose career ended after a dragon maimed her and cost her the lower part of her left leg.

Her replacement leg is made from Fey-stone.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Perla loves details, rumors, old maps, strange visitors, and stories told by people who have actually gone somewhere dangerous.

She can often be found with her prosthetic leg propped comfortably on a chair or table while sharing a drink with travelers.

docs.title: The Toad
docs.text:
Perla rescued and restored the ruined mansion that became The Toad.

She has filled it with artwork, stories, unusual furniture, and employees she considers part business decision and part extended family.

Gerdga is her closest friend and manages most daily operations.

Perla also watches over her nephew Munchies, whose plans regularly require intervention.

docs.title: Reputation
docs.text:
Adventurers like Perla because she knows when a ridiculous story is still worth hearing.

She likes adventurers because they keep bringing her new ones.

docs.title: Vostin The Mighty
docs.text:
Vostin The Mighty commands the Aegis Legion garrison at Duskpoint outside Goslow.

He is stern, proud, and intensely loyal to the institution he serves. Vostin is not known for warmth, but neither is he casually cruel. He believes order is one of the few things keeping the inhabited parts of Saros from collapsing back into dangerous isolation.

docs.title: The Mighty
docs.text:
People in Goslow call him Vostin the Mighty partly because of his physical confidence and partly because he is rarely seen lowering himself before anyone.

The exceptions are General Ironclad and Queen Amara, both of whom receive an obedience from him that he offers almost no one else.

docs.title: Duties
docs.text:
Vostin oversees:

  • Duskpoint’s garrison
  • Legion policing around Goslow
  • Patrols on the roads near the city
  • Griffin patrols throughout the Goslow–Pyrris region
  • Military coordination with the approaches to The High Road

He is often seen in the air with a small griffin-mounted guard.

docs.title: Griffin Bond
docs.text:
Vostin claimed his griffin as a hatchling in Vy’Tungavor. The animal is his lifelong bonded companion rather than Legion property, and the two remain in regular proximity even when Vostin’s duties keep him at Duskpoint.

Their bond, care, equipment, and travel follow the traditions described in Griffin Riders.

docs.title: Reputation
docs.text:
Merchants appreciate that his patrols keep important routes moving. People who dislike the Legion see him as the local face of Crown power.

Vostin accepts neither opinion as especially relevant to his work.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
He answers ultimately to General Ironclad and holds Queen Amara in unusually high personal regard.

His relationship with other Legion commanders is professional rather than friendly. Captain Serin Holt of Port Quartz, in particular, considers Vostin too willing to interpret orders according to local circumstances.

docs.title: Grymswatch
docs.text:
Grymswatch is a fortified military town and one of the principal strongholds of The Aegis Legion. It stands watch over the southeastern approaches of Saros and exists primarily to contain the threat posed by Karastos and the pirate factions operating from that coast.

Almost everything in Grymswatch serves the garrison.

docs.title: Character
docs.text:
The town feels more like a fortress with civilian streets than a settlement that later acquired walls. Training yards, warehouses, barracks, signal stations, and repair sheds dominate the skyline.

Civilians are accustomed to inspections, drills, ration stores, and military schedules.

docs.title: Government
docs.text:
Grymswatch is governed under a military charter. Admiral Thainan commands the naval establishment and holds enormous practical authority, while Festin Dontel serves as his lieutenant and second in command.

The arrangement is tolerated because the town’s strategic purpose is defense rather than commerce.

docs.title: Trade and Economy
docs.text:
Grymswatch survives on:

  • Naval supply contracts
  • Ship repair
  • Fishing
  • Salted provisions
  • Weapons and armor maintenance
  • Timber and rope purchased from other settlements
  • Crown expenditure

Without the Legion, the settlement would be dramatically smaller.

docs.title: Travel and Connections
docs.text:
Karastos lies about a day away by coastal vessel. The difficult land journey takes roughly 3 days where usable, 3-4 days by wagon, or about 2 days mounted.

This short sea connection makes naval readiness more important than the land road and places Admiral Thainan under constant pressure to watch the pirate coast. See Saros - Distances, Travel, Trade, and Population for the canonical route model.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Mira’s Wall is the great central fortress and training ground. Coastal patrols, watch towers, naval vessels, and constant readiness against Bloodmarked raiders define life here.

docs.title: Places of Interest
docs.text: • Mira’s Wall — Legion headquarters and training fortress

docs.title: NPCs Found Here
docs.text: NPC Race Building Factions Admiral Thainan Human Mira’s Wall The Aegis Legion Festin Dontel Human Mira’s Wall The Aegis Legion

docs.title: Mira's Wall
docs.text: The main headquarters and training facility for The Aegis Legion. Mira’s Wall is a massive castle-like structure and the central figure standing tall amongst the few low peasant homes that make up Grymswatch.

docs.title: Local Importance
docs.text: The place is a familiar part of daily life and a useful point of reference for visitors. Its value comes from the ordinary work, meetings, and routines that happen there rather than from a single famous event.

docs.title: Admiral Thainan
docs.text: Admiral Thainan is the senior naval commander based at Grymswatch and one of the most powerful officers in The Aegis Legion.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Thainan directs naval patrols and military operations concerned with the southern coast, especially the threat posed by Karastos and pirate groups such as the Bloodmarked.

His command controls ships, supplies, crews, and the movement of military cargo across a wide stretch of Saros.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Thainan is disciplined, proud, and comfortable making hard decisions without seeking approval from the people affected by them.

Supporters describe him as decisive.

Enemies describe him as a man who treats civilian suffering as a number that can be justified after the fact.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
Festin Dontel serves as his lieutenant and trusted second.

Mirken Stanton considers Thainan a sworn enemy, and that hostility is well known among sailors who know either man.

docs.title: Reputation
docs.text:
In Legion circles, Thainan is respected for keeping pirate pressure away from settled coasts.

Outside those circles, stories about harsh seizures, aggressive patrols, and operations conducted with little explanation have made his name controversial.

docs.title: Festin Dontel
docs.text:
Festin Dontel is the principal lieutenant of Admiral Thainan at Mira’s Wall in Grymswatch.

Festin handles much of the administrative and operational work that allows Thainan’s naval command to function.

docs.title: Duties
docs.text:
He coordinates:

  • Crew assignments
  • Patrol schedules
  • Supply requests
  • Ship readiness
  • Officer briefings
  • Orders moving between shore and fleet

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Festin is organized, loyal, and much less theatrical than the Admiral he serves.

He has learned to translate Thainan’s broad decisions into detailed orders that captains can actually follow.

People seeking access to the Admiral often discover that convincing Festin is the real first step.

docs.title: Isoltide
docs.text:
Isoltide stands opposite Albyrt on the great southern lake, where the eastern forest, river traffic, and lake fisheries meet.

The two cities depend on one another but maintain distinct laws, officials, guilds, and local pride.

docs.title: Character
docs.text: Isoltide is greener and more wooded than Albyrt. Timber structures, fish smokehouses, ferry slips, and forest roads crowd the lakeshore.

docs.title: Government
docs.text:
Teren Moss serves as the current East Reeve, presiding over a charter council representing ferry owners, fishers, forest trades, and established families.

The council coordinates closely with Albyrt on lake safety while arguing constantly over tolls and commercial precedence.

docs.title: Trade and Economy
docs.text:
• Lake fishing
  • Timber and forest goods
  • Ferry traffic
  • River cargo
  • Grain and food arriving from nearby farmland
  • Warehousing for goods crossing the lake

docs.title: Travel and Connections
docs.text:
Albyrt lies across the great southern lake. A ferry or lake boat crosses in less than a day; the road around takes about 2 days walking or 2-3 days by heavy cart.

Mysha lies roughly 65-80 road miles away: 3-4 days walking, 4-6 by wagon, or 2-3 days mounted. Navigable water movement can rival or beat the road.

See Saros - Distances, Travel, Trade, and Population for the canonical route model.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Isoltide is modestly fortified and maintains armed watch boats. The forest edge is patrolled because predators and older dangers can approach the town more quietly than any army.

docs.title: Places of Interest
docs.text:
• Eastwater Hall — civic hall and ferry registry
  • Isoltide Fishstairs — stepped fish market descending toward the lake
  • The Green Lantern — travelers’ inn near the forest road

docs.title: NPCs Found Here
docs.text: NPC Race Building Factions Teren Moss Half-Elf Eastwater Hall

docs.title: Eastwater Hall
docs.text: Eastwater Hall is the ferry registry and civic hall of Isoltide, where Teren Moss and the local council conduct business.

docs.title: Public Use
docs.text: Most residents encounter the building through ordinary civic business rather than ceremony. Notices, disputes, permits, records, and requests for local officials all pass through it, making the place a useful measure of what the settlement currently considers important.

docs.title: Lake Coordination
docs.text:
Eastwater Hall exchanges weather and ferry information with Albyrt across the lake.

Even during political disputes, both cities usually continue sharing storm warnings and missing-vessel reports. Nobody profits when a ferry sinks to prove a point about tolls.

docs.title: Isoltide Fishstairs
docs.text: The Isoltide Fishstairs are steep stone market terraces where catches are sorted, salted, and sold within sight of the lake. The stairs are washed repeatedly each day and still smell unmistakably of fish.

docs.title: Everyday Use
docs.text: Trade here follows the rhythms of arrivals and departures rather than a fixed modern schedule. Prices can change sharply when a caravan, fishing fleet, or shipment is late, and local information often moves between stalls faster than it reaches any official notice board.

docs.title: The Green Lantern
docs.text: The Green Lantern sits near the forest road into Isoltide. Foresters, ferrymen, and travelers use it as a meeting point before deciding whether to continue by road or cross the lake.

docs.title: Everyday Use
docs.text: The establishment serves as more than a place to drink or sleep. Travelers use it to hear road conditions, find temporary help, arrange meetings, and learn which local businesses are actually open to strangers.

docs.title: Waypoint
docs.text:
The Green Lantern is commonly used as a staging point for travelers deciding between the forest road and lake passage.

Stable space, packed meals, local weather advice, and introductions to ferry crews are as important to the business as beds.

docs.title: Teren Moss
docs.text:
Teren Moss serves as East Reeve of Isoltide.

A former timber factor with deep family ties to the lakeshore, Teren is comfortable negotiating with ferrymen, fishers, foresters, and merchants who all believe their problems should be solved first.

Teren has a friendly public rivalry with Mara Avelin of Albyrt. Their arguments over tolls and ferry schedules are famous enough to be repeated in taverns, but both understand that the twin cities depend on one another.

docs.title: Reputation
docs.text: Teren’s rivalry with Mara Avelin of Albyrt is real but mostly civic theater. Both leaders understand that a serious failure of ferry service or lake security hurts both cities at once.

docs.title: Karastos
docs.text:
Karastos is a notorious pirate-held port on the southeastern coast and one of the few major settlements that does not pretend to answer to the Crown.

Its population is difficult to count. Crews arrive, disappear, recruit, die, and sail again constantly; an estimate of roughly five thousand permanent residents is useful only in the broadest sense.

docs.title: Character
docs.text:
Karastos is loud, dangerous, crowded, and commercially useful. Stolen cargo can become ordinary merchandise within a few transactions, provided the right people are paid.

Its reputation for complete lawlessness is exaggerated. Karastos has rules—the difference is that they are enforced by captains, crews, local bosses, and whoever currently possesses enough force to make a ruling matter.

docs.title: Trade and Economy
docs.text:
• Pirated cargo
  • Ship repair and refitting
  • Smuggling
  • Coastal fishing
  • Weapons and provisions
  • Captive labor and illicit trade
  • Information about shipping routes

docs.title: Travel and Connections
docs.text:
Grymswatch is close enough to remain a constant military threat. The difficult land journey takes roughly 3 days where usable, 3-4 days by wagon, or about 2 days mounted. A coastal vessel can make the passage in about a day.

The ease of movement by sea makes patrols, raids, smuggling, and sudden changes in naval pressure more important than the apparent overland separation. See Saros - Distances, Travel, Trade, and Population for the canonical route model.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
There is no central civic watch comparable to Goslow’s. Individual docks, taverns, compounds, and warehouses employ their own guards.

The city’s greatest external threat is Grymswatch and the Aegis Legion fleet.

Bloodmarked crews are among the most feared pirate factions associated with the southern waters.

docs.title: NPCs Found Here
docs.text: NPC Race Building Factions

docs.title: Kylor
docs.text:
Kylor is a lonely logging and fishing town on the northwestern edge of the settled coast. Dense forest presses close behind the town while cold water and broken shoreline hem it in from the west.

Unlike Goslow, Kylor does not feel like a place people casually pass through. Most visitors came for timber, fish, work, or because they had nowhere easier to go.

docs.title: Character
docs.text:
The settlement smells of pitch, salt, smoke, sawdust, and wet rope.

People are accustomed to long absences. Logging crews vanish into the forest for weeks, fishing boats stay out through bad weather, and a household learning not to panic at an overdue family member is almost a local rite of passage.

docs.title: Government
docs.text:
The Kylor Moot governs local affairs under Derran Pike, the Harbor Reeve.

Logging families, boat owners, fishers, and timber factors dominate civic decisions. The Aegis Legion keeps a small presence, but Kylor values practical protection far more than outside supervision.

docs.title: Trade and Economy
docs.text:
Kylor exports:

  • Ship timber and heavy beams
  • Barrel staves
  • Charcoal
  • Pitch and resin
  • Smoked and salted fish
  • Rope fiber
  • Small coastal craft
  • Forest products

Much of the best timber eventually reaches Goslow.

docs.title: Travel and Connections
docs.text:
Goslow lies roughly 45-50 road miles away: 2-3 days walking, 3-4 days by heavy wagon, or 1.5-2 days mounted. A coastal vessel can make the trip in about a day in good conditions, so the heaviest timber usually moves by water.

Commercial cargo bound for Port Quartz normally passes through Goslow and changes vessels or transport there. The full journey commonly takes 3-5 days, depending on loading and weather.

See Saros - Distances, Travel, Trade, and Population for the canonical route model.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Kylor is protected by a stout timber palisade, coastal watch fires, armed logging crews, local boats, and a modest Legion detachment.

The most common serious threat is not an army. It is whatever emerges from the forest after a camp stops answering signals.

docs.title: Places of Interest
docs.text:
• The Drowning Mermaid — the oldest tavern in Kylor
  • Blackpine Yard — the largest saw yard and log boom
  • Lantern Head — coastal watch post and storm beacon
  • Saltwood Market — fish, timber contracts, rope, pitch, and forest goods

docs.title: NPCs Found Here
docs.text: NPC Race Building Factions Derran Pike Human Saltwood Market Kylor Moot Mara Venn Human The Drowning Mermaid Osk Fen Half-Orc Blackpine Yard

docs.title: Blackpine Yard
docs.text:
Blackpine Yard is the largest saw yard and log boom in Kylor.

Timber floated down from forest camps is chained, graded, cut, and prepared for coastal shipment. Osk Fen works from the yard when he is not in the woods.

Much of the best timber eventually reaches Goslow for shipbuilding.

docs.title: Workday
docs.text: The site is busiest when goods are arriving, being processed, or being prepared for transport. Laborers, haulers, inspectors, and specialist craftspeople all depend on the work staying organized, so strangers wandering through active areas are noticed quickly.

docs.title: Lantern Head
docs.text:
Lantern Head is the coastal watch post above Kylor.

Its beacon warns of storms, missing boats, pirate sightings, and emergencies at logging camps close enough to signal the coast.

A small Aegis Legion detachment shares the post with local watchmen.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: The structure is part of the settlement’s ordinary defensive routine, not merely a wartime monument. Watch rotations, inspections, signal procedures, and emergency stores are maintained even during quiet seasons.

docs.title: Saltwood Market
docs.text:
Saltwood Market is the commercial center of Kylor and the usual meeting place of Derran Pike and the Kylor Moot when business spills beyond formal sessions.

Fish, rope, pitch, charcoal, tools, and timber contracts dominate the stalls.

News from Goslow often arrives here several days before it reaches the logging camps.

docs.title: Everyday Use
docs.text: Trade here follows the rhythms of arrivals and departures rather than a fixed modern schedule. Prices can change sharply when a caravan, fishing fleet, or shipment is late, and local information often moves between stalls faster than it reaches any official notice board.

docs.title: The Drowning Mermaid
docs.text:
The Drowning Mermaid is the oldest tavern in Kylor and the first place most outsiders hear the town’s real news.

Mara Venn runs the Mermaid with a practical tolerance for loggers, fishers, Legion patrols, and travelers who know when to stop asking questions.

The walls are covered in broken figureheads, storm-damaged signs, and pieces of boats that never returned intact.

docs.title: Everyday Use
docs.text: The establishment serves as more than a place to drink or sleep. Travelers use it to hear road conditions, find temporary help, arrange meetings, and learn which local businesses are actually open to strangers.

docs.title: Derran Pike
docs.text:
Derran Pike is the Harbor Reeve of Kylor and chairs the Kylor Moot.

He spent most of his life moving timber rafts and fishing boats before taking office.

Derran values the Aegis Legion when something dangerous comes out of the forest, but resents officers who treat Kylor like a distant dependency of Goslow.

He judges most policy by one question: will it keep the camps supplied through winter?

docs.title: Manner
docs.text: Derran speaks like a working harbor man even in council meetings. He values people who can explain the practical cost of a proposal and distrusts policies built entirely from maps drawn in warmer offices.

docs.title: Mara Venn
docs.text:
Mara Venn owns The Drowning Mermaid, the oldest tavern in Kylor.

Mara knows which logging crews are overdue, which captains are lying about storms, and which strangers arrived without a believable reason to be so far northwest.

She is hospitable without being trusting.

docs.title: Reputation
docs.text: Mara is a reliable source of practical town gossip because crews talk freely in front of an innkeeper they have known for years. She rarely repeats a confidence without a reason, but she remembers everything.

docs.title: Osk Fen
docs.text:
Osk Fen is a logging boss and forest pathfinder working out of Blackpine Yard in Kylor.

He has survived more vanished camps and bad winters than most of the town’s foresters.

Osk is especially wary of unexplained silence in the woods. He claims a forest full of predators should never be completely quiet.

docs.title: Manner
docs.text: Osk is terse with strangers and patient with inexperienced workers who admit what they do not know. He has no tolerance for boasting in the forest, where confidence does nothing to improve a bad trail or falling tree.

docs.title: Lilya
docs.text:
Lilya presses against the lower slopes of The Silvervein Summits, built as close to the mountain as its miners can safely live. Retaining walls, ore yards, smoke stacks, hoists, steep streets, and tunnel mouths make the town appear wedged into the range rather than placed beside it.

Its reason for existing is simple: the mountain pays.

docs.title: Character
docs.text:
Lilya is industrious, cramped, and perpetually dusty. Work shifts shape the day more than the sun does. Bells announce cave-ins, shift changes, fires, and closures, and almost every household has lost someone below ground.

Miners tend to measure trust by competence. A stranger who can shore a tunnel, repair a pump, or carry an injured worker earns respect faster than someone with an impressive title.

docs.title: Government
docs.text:
The Stone Council governs the town under Crown charter. Maela Torr, the Stone Reeve, chairs the council and represents Lilya in major civic disputes.

The council is strongly influenced by mine crews, smelters, haulers, craftsmen, and long-established households.

The Aegis Legion maintains a small defensive presence because the mines are strategically important, but local mine law predates many current Crown regulations and is fiercely protected.

docs.title: Trade and Economy
docs.text:
Lilya exports:

  • Silver-bearing ore
  • Iron and lesser metals
  • Cut stone
  • Tools and fittings
  • Pigments and mineral salts
  • Deep-earth materials
  • Durable goods prepared for the fall-cask trade

Most ordinary freight moves south by road to Trystn, where it can continue toward Port Quartz or Rore.

docs.title: Travel and Connections
docs.text:
Trystn lies roughly 60-70 road miles away: 3-4 days walking, 4-5 days by heavy wagon, or 2-3 days mounted.

The full safe route to Port Quartz runs through Trystn and covers approximately 110-120 road miles. It takes about 6 days walking, 7-9 days by heavy commercial wagon, or roughly 4 days mounted. A direct griffin journey can be made in about a day.

Ore, stone, and finished mineral goods move downhill. Food, feed, timber, tools, and mine supplies move north. See Saros - Distances, Travel, Trade, and Population for the canonical route model.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Lilya relies on:

  • Heavy gates
  • Stone watch positions
  • Armed mine crews
  • A small Legion detachment
  • Controlled mine entrances
  • Emergency refuge chambers cut into the mountain

A disaster below ground is often more dangerous than an enemy outside the walls.

docs.title: Places of Interest
docs.text:
• Stonewake Hall — meeting place of the Stone Council
  • The Silver Gate — the most heavily controlled entrance into the principal mine works
  • Hammerfall Yard — ore sorting, smelting, repair, and loading
  • The Deep Lantern — miners’ inn and hiring hall

The oldest and deepest workings around Lilya overlap with forgotten dwarven construction whose full extent is no longer understood.

docs.title: NPCs Found Here

docs.title: Hammerfall Yard
docs.text:
Hammerfall Yard is the loud industrial center of Lilya.

Ore is weighed, sorted, broken, smelted, loaded, and argued over here. Wagons bound for Trystn form in the yard, while specially reinforced barrels intended for the fall-cask route toward Port Quartz are inspected nearby.

The yard never truly becomes quiet.

docs.title: Workday
docs.text: The site is busiest when goods are arriving, being processed, or being prepared for transport. Laborers, haulers, inspectors, and specialist craftspeople all depend on the work staying organized, so strangers wandering through active areas are noticed quickly.

docs.title: Stonewake Hall
docs.text:
Stonewake Hall is the civic meeting house of Lilya and the seat of Maela Torr and the Stone Council.

The hall is built against the mountain itself. Its rear wall is exposed stone covered with old survey marks and memorial names.

Mine disputes, ration decisions, road contracts, and emergency closures are argued here.

docs.title: Local Importance
docs.text: The place is a familiar part of daily life and a useful point of reference for visitors. Its value comes from the ordinary work, meetings, and routines that happen there rather than from a single famous event.

docs.title: The Deep Lantern
docs.text:
The Deep Lantern is the largest inn and miners’ hiring hall in Lilya.

Prospectors, haulers, surveyors, and off-shift miners exchange contracts and rumors here.

Ysra Pell is a regular, and recent talk increasingly concerns dead herbs, sealed lower works, and strange lights beneath The Silvervein Summits.

docs.title: Everyday Use
docs.text: The establishment serves as more than a place to drink or sleep. Travelers use it to hear road conditions, find temporary help, arrange meetings, and learn which local businesses are actually open to strangers.

docs.title: The Silver Gate
docs.text:
The Silver Gate is the most heavily controlled entrance into the primary mine works of Lilya.

Garran Flint oversees access, safety records, shift closures, and the locking of shafts considered too unstable for ordinary workers.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
The gate is built into an older stone opening reinforced repeatedly by later Sarosian construction.

Equipment checks, worker tallies, and emergency bells make the entrance feel more like a fortress checkpoint than a normal mine mouth.

docs.title: Deeper Workings
docs.text:
Some older passages below the active mines are clearly dwarven and extend toward parts of The Silvervein Summits no current survey fully explains.

Most miners have no reason to go near them.

docs.title: Garran Flint
docs.text:
Garran Flint is the master of The Silver Gate, the most heavily controlled mine entrance in Lilya.

He is one of the few dwarves in town willing to discuss old workings beneath The Silvervein Summits, though he becomes evasive when asked how deep those passages truly go.

Garran has noticed old stonework vibrating faintly at night and has quietly barred several lower passages from ordinary miners.

docs.title: Manner
docs.text: Garran trusts stone more readily than rumors. If he closes a passage, he expects miners to stay out until he personally changes the order. His willingness to admit that some older dwarven work exceeds his understanding earns him more respect than false certainty would.

docs.title: Maela Torr
docs.text:
Maela Torr is the current Stone Reeve of Lilya and chairs the Stone Council.

She comes from a family of mine surveyors rather than mine owners and has a reputation for knowing exactly how much ore, food, timber, and labor the town can spare before a promise becomes impossible.

Maela respects The Aegis Legion when it keeps roads and mine entrances safe, but she opposes military interference in local mine law.

The recent problems beneath The Silvervein Summits have made her increasingly suspicious of sealed orders arriving from outside Lilya.

docs.title: Manner
docs.text: Maela dislikes promises that do not include numbers. A plan that cannot explain how much timber, food, rope, labor, or time it requires is not yet a plan in her view.

docs.title: Ysra Pell
docs.text:
Ysra Pell is a prospector and field surveyor based in Lilya.

She spends more time beyond the comfortable limits of the active mines than most respectable mine masters consider wise.

docs.title: Work
docs.text:
Ysra surveys:

  • New mineral traces
  • Unstable slopes
  • Abandoned shafts
  • Springs and underground water
  • Old stonework exposed by fresh digging
  • Plant and animal changes around prospecting sites

She is particularly useful because she records things that do not immediately look profitable.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Ysra is stubborn, curious, and willing to write down observations other people dismiss as superstition.

Mine managers sometimes call her alarmist. Younger prospectors tend to listen to her because she has returned alive from places where more confident surveyors did not.

docs.title: Communication
docs.text: Ysra has used road couriers, merchant caravans, and even fall casks when she believed information needed to leave the mountain country without relying on a single local messenger.

docs.title: Mysha
docs.text: Mysha is a southern logging town set where river, forest, and open land meet. Halflings are especially common in the settlement, and many local families maintain stories connecting their ancestors to Lake Runa.

docs.title: Character
docs.text: Mysha is low-built, communal, and deeply tied to the forest. Sawmills and river booms sit beside gardens, workshops, and stone yards.

docs.title: Government
docs.text: A small Woodward Council manages cutting rights, river use, fire prevention, and disputes between logging crews. Pellin Root currently acts as Speaker.

docs.title: Trade and Economy
docs.text:
Mysha depends primarily on logging, but also produces:

  • Carved goods
  • Charcoal
  • River timber
  • Small amounts of quarried stone
  • Tools and practical crafts
  • Food from nearby farms and gardens
  • Smoke Leaf, including the halfling-grown varieties considered the finest in Saros

Much of its timber moves by river before joining southern trade routes.

docs.title: Travel and Connections
docs.text:
Isoltide lies roughly 65-80 road miles away: 3-4 days walking, 4-6 by wagon, or 2-3 days mounted. Water travel can be faster where the connected channels are navigable.

Soryn’s Crossing lies roughly 45-55 miles away: 2-3 days walking, 3-4 by wagon, about 2 days mounted, or 1-2 days for river freight when conditions cooperate.

See Saros - Distances, Travel, Trade, and Population for the canonical route model.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: The town relies on local wardens, organized work crews, and a militia accustomed to forest emergencies. Fire is treated as seriously as monsters.

docs.title: Places of Interest
docs.text:
• Rootwheel Mill — largest sawmill and river wheel
  • Runa House — communal hall associated with local halfling traditions
  • The Split Log — rough inn used by crews and river traders

docs.title: NPCs Found Here
docs.text: NPC Race Building Factions Pellin Root Halfling Runa House

docs.title: Rootwheel Mill
docs.text: Rootwheel Mill is the largest sawmill in Mysha, driven by a heavy river wheel and surrounded by log booms. Much of the town’s commercial timber passes through the mill before continuing downstream.

docs.title: Workday
docs.text: The site is busiest when goods are arriving, being processed, or being prepared for transport. Laborers, haulers, inspectors, and specialist craftspeople all depend on the work staying organized, so strangers wandering through active areas are noticed quickly.

docs.title: Runa House
docs.text: Runa House is a communal hall in Mysha associated with local halfling families and their traditions concerning Lake Runa. Pellin Root often conducts council business here.

docs.title: Public Use
docs.text: Most residents encounter the building through ordinary civic business rather than ceremony. Notices, disputes, permits, records, and requests for local officials all pass through it, making the place a useful measure of what the settlement currently considers important.

docs.title: Community Role
docs.text:
Runa House hosts meals, family meetings, seasonal observances, and discussions about forest use.

Objects and stories associated with Lake Runa are kept in several rooms, though residents do not treat the building as a museum for curious strangers.

docs.title: The Split Log
docs.text: The Split Log is a rough crew inn in Mysha where loggers and river traders eat cheaply, sleep heavily, and compare injuries.

docs.title: Everyday Use
docs.text: The establishment serves as more than a place to drink or sleep. Travelers use it to hear road conditions, find temporary help, arrange meetings, and learn which local businesses are actually open to strangers.

docs.title: Clientele
docs.text:
The common room fills earliest when logging crews come off shift and latest when river traders are waiting on water levels.

Work is often hired informally over meals, and newcomers looking for a guide, cutter, teamster, or spare pair of hands usually ask here before visiting any formal office.

docs.title: Pellin Root
docs.text:
Pellin Root is the current Speaker of Mysha’s Woodward Council.

He is a broad, weathered halfling with an unusually soft voice and a deep familiarity with timber rights, river levels, and the old family stories connecting Mysha’s halflings to Lake Runa.

Pellin prefers negotiated cutting boundaries over punishment. His patience ends quickly when a logging crew ignores fire restrictions or fells marked trees.

docs.title: Reputation
docs.text: Pellin is well liked by crews who obey cutting rules and deeply unpopular with anyone caught burning slash carelessly. His knowledge of the river and older halfling stories makes him useful beyond ordinary council work.

docs.title: Port Quartz
docs.text:
Port Quartz is one of the great transfer points of northern Saros, built around an immense river crossing that cannot be bridged by present-day Sarosian engineering. Ferries, cargo craft, warehouses, customs offices, and river crews shape nearly every part of daily life.

The town is also the last dependable concentration of civilization for anyone turning northwest toward The Masys Mountains.

docs.title: Geography and Routes
docs.text:
The principal safe commercial road runs east toward Trystn, where freight can continue north toward Lilya or southeast toward Rore.

There is no ordinary safe commercial road southwest to Goslow or Kylor. Enormous rivers divide the regions. The normal Goslow connection is a shipping route through Bishop’s Bay and then upstream to Port Quartz.

There is no charted safe road north from Port Quartz to Lake of Lament.

The lake lies far above Port Quartz in the high basin around The Silvervein Summits. At its southwestern edge, the water plunges over an enormous cataract before joining the river that eventually reaches Port Quartz. No ordinary vessel can travel upstream through that fall.

Explorers may cross west at Westwater Ferry and turn toward the Masys country, but maintained paths disappear quickly.

docs.title: Travel and Connections
docs.text:
Destination Route Working Distance and Time Goslow River and coastal shipping 70-90 water miles; ordinarily 2-3 days toward Port Quartz and 1-2 days returning Trystn Maintained road 45-50 miles; 2-3 days walking or 3-4 by heavy wagon Lilya Via Trystn 110-120 road miles; about 6 days walking or 7-9 by heavy commercial wagon Masys country Westwater Ferry and unmaintained routes Expedition travel; no dependable commercial time

See Saros - Distances, Travel, Trade, and Population for the canonical route model.

docs.title: Government
docs.text:
Port Quartz is governed under royal charter by the Mooring Council, presided over by Hesta Vane, the First Mooring.

The local Aegis Legion garrison is commanded by Captain Serin Holt. The garrison protects the crossing and regional routes, but it does not legally govern the town.

The disappearance of Queen Amara has made the boundary between civic and military authority increasingly important.

docs.title: Trade and Economy
docs.text:
Port Quartz makes most of its wealth by moving, storing, insuring, and recovering goods.

Major trades include:

  • Ferry operation
  • Warehousing and customs
  • Cargo brokerage
  • Rivercraft repair
  • Cartage and animal handling
  • Rope, pitch, tackle, and cooperage
  • Salvage
  • Expedition supply
  • Trade moving between Goslow, Trystn, Lilya, and Rore

One of the strangest parts of the economy is the fall-cask trade. Durable goods from Lilya and the Lake of Lament basin can be packed into reinforced barrels and intentionally sent over the great waterfall for recovery downstream.

See fall-cask trade for construction, registration, recovery fees, and the claim laws governing lost or unclaimed casks.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Port Quartz has several overlapping security forces:

  • The civic Chain Watch
  • The local Aegis Legion garrison
  • Licensed private guards employed by merchants and warehouse owners
  • A militia that can be raised during a serious emergency

The town’s greatest everyday hazards are river accidents, cargo theft, smuggling, and disputes that become violent before anyone agrees who has jurisdiction.

docs.title: Places of Interest
docs.text:
• The Fourty Knights — the largest tavern and inn in town, operated by Prance Mondrel
  • Hall of Moorings — civic hall, customs house, and seat of Hesta Vane
  • White Quays — the pale commercial waterfront
  • Cataract Yard — fall-cask recovery and salvage works
  • Vane Archive — expedition journals and maps kept by Nelra Vossin
  • Westwater Ferry — the main western crossing, overseen by Oren Bale
  • Breakwater Registry — licenses guides, surveyors, ferry crews, and declared expeditions
  • Quartz Vaults — secured warehouses cut into pale stone
  • Shrine of the Last Oar — riverside memorial to those lost on the water
  • Chainwatch — civic watch tower and ferry signal station
  • The Quartz Cobra — chartered gambling hall and Bank of Saros, operated by Lind Bergy

docs.title: Character
docs.text:
Port Quartz is crowded, loud, practical, and accustomed to strangers. Its people respect competence more than titles.

The river decides working hours, prices, law, and funerals. No government has ever persuaded it otherwise.
